subject: On-prem IaC off-ramp: module split, CI parity & network evidence
messages:
From: Timothy Li <tim.li@acmefin.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureOps <procureops@acmefin.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: On-prem IaC off-ramp — module split + CI parity + network evidence

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are moving toward a proof-of-concept to run Redwood Private in our on-prem environment and the architects here asked for a short review focused on three items before we can sign off:

1) Clear module boundaries — they'd like Terraform/Helm/Ansible split so our SBX and PROD on-prem clusters can consume only the networking and runtime modules they need.
2) CI parity — we need a CI pipeline that mirrors your hosted deploy logic (image signing, artifact provenance, and gating) so we can pass our internal change control.
3) Network evidence — VPC routing diagrams, eBPF/loadbalancer placement, and an audit of default deny rules for the on-prem install.

Can your infra team provide a short review and an artifact bundle (diffs + diagrams + CI snippets) we can hand to our compliance folks? We are targeting a decision meeting on 2026-09-25.

Attaching the current runbook we have for vendor-offramp for context.

Thanks,
Timothy

Subject: Re: Request: On-prem IaC off-ramp — module split + CI parity + network evidence

Tessa / Team / Timothy —

Thanks for the sync this morning. Per notes below, attached are the artifacts I promised: a focused diff that extracts the networking pieces into a standalone terraform module (iac-module-split.diff) and a network-zone-diagram-v2.svg that maps the proposed on-prem routing and eBPF placement. Summary of changes & rationale:

- terraform/networking/ -> modules/networking-onprem/
  - isolates routing, subnet creation, and NSG-equivalent rules (keeps provider-agnostic variables).
- helm/values-networking.yaml -> chart values now accept "networkProvider: onprem" to avoid hostPath assumptions in the existing charts.
- ansible/playbooks/bastion.yml unchanged; added conditional role for airgapped artifact staging.

Security / compliance highlights (short):
- Default-deny applied at module entry points; explicit allow lists for kube-apiserver, bastion, and LB health checks.
- KV caching and secrets are left to the customer's KMS in Private mode; we added a docs stub showing our recommended KMS mappings.

Attachments referenced (stubs):
- iac-module-split.diff (text/patch)
- network-zone-diagram-v2.svg (image/svg+xml)

Inline note: The diff intentionally keeps the original modules as a migration path — we add a switch param: "use_separate_network_module = true". That should make adoption non-disruptive for teams that want incremental rollout.

Grace

Timothy — quick note on CI parity artifacts (attached: ci-pipeline-parity-snippet.yml):

- We provide a small GH Actions / GitLab snippet that you can drop into your pipeline. Primary checks:
  - image-signature-verify: validates signed images using cosign (our images are signed; snippet shows verification step).
  - provenance-check: verifies build provenance metadata (SBOM link, builder ID).
  - artifact-allowlist: a short task to ensure only approved helm charts/artifacts are published to your internal registry.

Implementation caveats: for air-gapped installs you'll need a mirror registry step; snippet shows a two-stage mirror + verify flow. We opted for cosign + intoto metadata verification so your change control can detect unsigned or unknown-build images.

Evidence checklist (short):
- network-zone-diagram (attached)
- module split diff (attached)
- CI parity snippet (attached)
- a short runbook item that shows the signing verification command to run during approvals

If ProcureOps needs a short note about artifact provenance and our default image-signing approach, Laura can draft language for the procurement packet.

Vivek

Hi —

Short answers to procurement questions:

1) Migration support estimate: If ACME chooses to adopt the separate network module immediately and needs a hands-on migration, we estimate 8-12 engineer-hours for a single cluster migration (includes runbook updates and one test run). If you keep dual-path (use_separate_network_module = true) migration is ad hoc and lower risk — ~3-4 hours to validate.

2) Delivery & licensing: We deliver the CI parity snippet as an example under MIT for you to copy into your pipelines. Any production integrations or supported runbook handoffs requiring Redwood engineering assistance are treated under the Private deployment support contract.

3) Procurement bullet (copyable):
"Redwood Private on-premise deployments rely on signed container images and verifiable build provenance. Customer is responsible for managing KMS/HSM for private key storage; Redwood provides integration guidance and example verification steps for inclusion in change-control workflows"

Next steps from our side: Tessa will bundle the artifacts and push the Drive folder link to you by 9/23 EOD, and Grace will prepare a short migration playbook snippet. Vivek and I will be available during the 9/25 decision meeting.
